### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/data-api.mdx`  _(via /:object/:id/clone (route, bridged from symbol cloneData — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx`  _(via cloneData (symbol, a method of class ProtocolDataCrudFacet))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via /:object/:id/clone (route, bridged from symbol cloneData — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via cloneData (symbol, a method of class ProtocolDataCrudFacet))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via /:object/:id/clone (route, bridged from symbol cloneData — its route source's handler names it))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1647fb3d74ba56b13fa54b1502a6b82c715bbb67` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f23f327adf1f767939ab573edcf460dc5384c6bb` — the merge of head `7666b5f79d5178ca19a243d35c63ad3ac49333e7` into base `1647fb3d74ba56b13fa54b1502a6b82c715bbb67`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f23f327adf1f767939ab573edcf460dc5384c6bb && git checkout f23f327adf1f767939ab573edcf460dc5384c6bb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1647fb3d74ba56b13fa54b1502a6b82c715bbb67 7666b5f79d5178ca19a243d35c63ad3ac49333e7 && git checkout -B drift-repro 1647fb3d74ba56b13fa54b1502a6b82c715bbb67 && git merge --no-ff 7666b5f79d5178ca19a243d35c63ad3ac49333e7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1647fb3d74ba56b13fa54b1502a6b82c715bbb67
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1647fb3d74ba56b13fa54b1502a6b82c715bbb67` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## L1 · PR #36063 · head `9fea83f403` · **ACCEPT** (CI not concluded) · 2026-11-21T12:19Z

Card #35721. Claim 7061812207, report 7062444705. Clause-② no and Metadata-protocol none. There is no spec, governed or narrowing face, so this PR owes no L2 (`contract-review.md` l.6–11). I read the whole diff against the merge base `8145424b53` (3 files, +250/−2) and the code it leans on.

### Route deviation: accepted
The card asked to normalise the expanded value back to an id. The dev instead reads the source with `RAW_FILE_VALUES_CONTEXT_KEY` spread onto the caller's context, and that is the better route:
- **The flag does one thing.** Its only engine consumer is `resolveFileReferences` (`engine-file-reference-hydration.ts:178`), which returns the stored rows unhydrated. So the clone gets the stored `sys_file` id, or the list of ids for a `multiple` field, for every `FILE_REFERENCE_TYPES` field.
- **It covers every expanded shape.** A converter on the consumer side would have needed to handle three shapes: the expanded object, the list of expanded objects, and the refused-reader `{ id, metadataRefused }` marker.
- **It is the spec-declared opt-out,** spelled exactly like `engine-validate.ts:427`.

### The side effect: no change to security or session reading
- **Security reads the same either way.** `findOne` passes the context straight through: `mergeReadContext` returns the options context as given, and every consumer reads it as `context?.x`. The security middleware's principal test is `isPrincipalLessContext` (`security-plugin.ts:619`), which checks `positions`, `permissions` and `userId`. Both `undefined` and `{ __rawFileValues: true }` are principal-less, and neither carries `isSystem`. So a call without a context goes down the same security path as before.
- **The one `context === undefined` branch is not on this path.** It is in `resolveSearchQueryableFields` (`engine-query-lowering.ts:306`), which applies only to `$search`, and the clone's `{ where: { id } }` has none.
- **The shape is already common.** `engine-validate.ts:427` builds this exact context for the pre-image read of every by-id update made without a context.
- **Raw ids add nothing to what the caller can read.** The source read is never returned to the caller; it only fills the insert payload. The refused-reader marker already carried the id. The insert's field-reference rule (`file-reference-lifecycle.ts`, #25692 / #26043) asks the download door's verdict for the write's caller before any copy. A file the caller may not read is refused at the field with `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` and is never copied, the same rule an `overrides` id already met. Because read access comes from the parent record, a caller who can read the source can download its own files anyway, so the copy adds nothing.
- **Insert context is unchanged.** The insert still runs with the caller's `ctx`, or none: the code only removed `ctxOpt`. A call without a context therefore copies "as before", per that module's own docblock.

### Evidence
- **Red on main, green on the fix.** The bug reproduced on main: `protocol-data-crud.ts` was restored byte-for-byte, and the REST pin answered 400 "expected string, received object" for single `file`, `multiple` file and `image`, while the CONTROL using `overrides` answered 201. With the fix the pin passes 3 of 3; with base restored, 2 fail. The ablation through `ablation-replace.mjs` turns 2 red and restores blob-equal.
- **What the pin covers.** It drives the real door end to end: presign, PUT, complete, then clone. It covers a clone with no body (every file field gets a new id owned by the clone's slot, holding the source's bytes, and the source keeps its file), and it covers `overrides` still winning, including `papers: null`.
- **Changeset.** I checked it sentence by sentence. Every sentence matches the code and the pins.
- **File surface.** The diff is inside the claim: `cloneData`, one REST-door pin and one patch changeset. `engine.ts` is untouched.

### Nits (no re-review needed)
- **N1. Unpinned refusal arm.** A clone whose source file the caller may not read now reaches the #26043 field refusal without any `overrides`. In practice that needs an object whose `fileAccessDelegate` names another object. Nothing pins it on the clone door. One dogfood case asserting `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`, the field-level `invalid_value` entry and no copy would close it, here or in a follow-up.
- **N2. Changeset omission.** A clone with no body can now reach `500 FileReferenceCopyError` when the source's stored content is missing; before, only the `overrides` path could. The Acceptance notes say so, but the changeset does not. One clause would make the release note complete.
- **N3. Runner claim corrected.** `dispatch-gates --ran` printed "0 NOT-MEASURED". The dev's exit-3 reading of `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` corrects that to 1, as reported. CI's lint lane owns that gate.

### Owed
- **CI at `9fea83f403`:** 14 success, 16 skipped, 21 in progress at this stamp (Test Core 1–10, Build Core, every Type Check, the lints). It has not concluded. This ACCEPT holds on this head once CI is green.
- **The dogfood pin's only witness before merge is the dev's local run.** The `Dogfood Regression Gate` first runs in the merge queue, so read it there.

## Delta L1 · PR #36063 · head `7666b5f79d` · **ACCEPT** (CI not concluded) · 2026-11-21T13:18Z

Previous verdict: ACCEPT 7062486589 @`9fea83f403`, conditional on CI. The head moved fast-forward by two commits (`3bcd9d88`, `7666b5f7`). Delta report 7063166004. Diff: 2 files, +14/−2. `protocol-data-crud.ts` is byte-identical to the head I accepted.

### Correction to my previous L1
CI at `9fea83f403` went red: `Test Core (4/10)` failed. The objectql unit pin `protocol-data.test.ts` › cloneData › "forwards context to findOne and insert" asserted `findOne(…, objectContaining({ context: ctx }))`, which the fix changes on purpose. I did not look for existing `cloneData` pins outside the PR's own files. The dev's local run covered metadata-protocol only. My "ACCEPT once CI is green" therefore never held at that head. From now on, when a diff changes a call's arguments, I grep for existing pins on that callee across packages.

### Delta: met
- **findOne pin is now exact.** It asserts `findOne('account', { where: { id: 'src-1' }, context: { userId: 'u1', [RAW_FILE_VALUES_CONTEXT_KEY]: true } })` by deep equality, not `objectContaining`. Any other key added to the read context would fail it.
- **The caller's context is untouched.** `expect(ctx).toEqual({ userId: 'u1' })` proves the key went onto a copy.
- **Insert pin unchanged.** It still asserts `context: ctx` by deep equality, so the insert runs with the caller's own context and without the key. That is the side-effect reading I verified in 7062486589, now pinned at unit level.
- **Typecheck fix is clean.** The `insert.mock.calls[0][2]` read that broke `check:test-typecheck` at `3bcd9d88` was removed, not cast or `@ts-expect-error`ed. Its proof is carried by the two deep-equality assertions above.
- **N2 is carried.** The changeset's added sentence says a clone with no body now reaches the copy step's `500 FileReferenceCopyError` when stored bytes are missing, as `overrides` already did. The sentence matches the code.
- **N1 declined, and that is acceptable.** A refusal pin needs a second member who can read the record but not its file (a `fileAccessDelegate` object), which is more fixture than this card. It should be filed as its own test card, so the #26043 arm on the clone door gets a witness.

### Owed
- **Claim amendment.** `packages/objectql/src/protocol-data.test.ts` is outside the claim's file surface (metadata-protocol `cloneData`, one REST-door pin, one changeset). The edit is the pin the fix necessarily changes, but it needs a one-line amendment record on the card.
- **CI at `7666b5f79d`:** 31 success, 16 skipped, 6 in progress at this stamp, and no failure so far. This ACCEPT holds on this head once CI is green.
- **The `Dogfood Regression Gate`** runs first in the merge queue. Read it there.
